competitors.name: Screamin' Sicilian / Palermo's
competitors.action: Screamin' Sicilian now appears to be active at Target in a deli-adjacent Roman-style take-and-bake format, not just the classic frozen door. That is a meaningful channel move because it lets a premium frozen brand borrow some of the freshness theater of prepared foods while staying in grocery convenience territory.

competitors.name: Food Lion
competitors.action: Food Lion's private-label frozen pizza push now looks more premium and flavor-forward than a generic value-line expansion, with reported SKUs including cup-and-char uncured pepperoni with hot honey plus sausage and caramelized onion. That sharpens the earlier shelf-pressure signal: retailer-owned pizza is not just scaling, it is learning premium language and trend cues too.

competitors.name: Aldi / Walmart private label / Richelieu Foods
competitors.action: The salmonella-linked frozen pizza issue remains one of the highest-signal operational stories in the aisle because it spread across multiple private-label programs through a shared dry-milk ingredient. Even though the alert first surfaced earlier this month, continuing mainstream pickup keeps reinforcing the same lesson: upstream ingredient failures can quickly become multi-banner category damage.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza competition is getting harder to categorize cleanly by aisle or tier
trends.magnitude: Today's clearest signals were premium frozen brands crossing into deli-style presentation, private label borrowing premium flavor architecture, and safety issues still rippling across multiple retailer programs.
trends.context: Real Dough should assume the aisle is converging from both sides: premium brands are chasing fresher merchandising cues while value and private-label players are getting better at premium storytelling. That makes operational trust and a very clear sourdough claim even more important.

breaking.headline: The sharpest signal today is category convergence: premium brands are borrowing fresh-prepared cues, private label is borrowing premium flavor language, and supply-chain failures still cut across banners fast.
breaking.impact: For Real Dough, that means the moat cannot just be 'premium frozen pizza.' It needs to be specific: true sourdough process, clean operational trust, and a shelf story that reads instantly.
